summary: John Allan was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1902–1907) and Leipzig University (~1907–1908). He held posts at the British Museum from 1907, University College London (1907–1917), SOAS (1920–1922), and Edinburgh (1949–1955).

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst College, under William Dwight Whitney, and at Tübingen and Berlin. He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).
John B. Carman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 1999) and head of the Center for the Study of World Religions.

John B. Cobb Jr. is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He founded the Center for Process Studies and held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989).

John Berthrong was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who completed his graduate studies under Alfonso Verdu. He served on the faculty at Boston University from around 1989 to 2022.

John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Edinburgh. He was principal at Fort William College (1800–1804), taught for the East India Company, and was University College London's first Professor of Hindustani (~1828–1831).
John Brockington is an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh, with his post attested in 1987 and 2003.

John Brough studied at Edinburgh and St John's College under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he was Professor of Sanskrit at London (1948–1967) and later Professor at Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Virginia in 1982. He served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).
John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford (~1883–1887). He held a post at the University of St Andrews from circa 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist, linguist, and historian who studied at Oxford (~1946–1948). He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1948–1951) and SOAS University of London (~1953–1984).
John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a professorship at Ohio State University, attested between 1987 and 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held an appointment at the University of North Florida, attested in 1988, and later served as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy there (attested 2015).
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1790–1797). In 1808, he served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classicist educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at Oxford (~1946–1952) before serving as a lecturer and later Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics at Cambridge (1969–1984).

John Claude White was active in Tibetology and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876) before becoming an Assistant Engineer with the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

John Clifford Holt is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah at Chicago. He was Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (~1978–2018) and Numata Chair at the University of Calgary (2006).

John Collinson Nesfield studied at Merton College. Working in Indology and linguistics, he held professorships at Presidency College, Chennai and Krishnagar Government College, became principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878), and was a Fellow at Allahabad (1887).

John Corrigan is a religious studies and history scholar who earned his PhD from Chicago. He taught at Virginia, Harvard, and Arizona State before becoming a distinguished professor of religion and history at Florida State University (~2001).

John Crawfurd was an author in history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803). He served as an East India Company physician (1803–1808) and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.
